![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14059013/assets/118759b163a4410f66d5855d7b7b1fd9c2ee4be585e778a759997036bd95f765.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t)$ and $y=y(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2+y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s$ and $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2+t{e}^{s}, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =s{e}^{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂t} & =0, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂t} & ={e}^{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂t} \\  & =(2+t{e}^{s})(0)+(s{e}^{s})({e}^{s}) \\  & =s{e}^{2s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Let f(x,y)=2x+xy, where x=ses and y=tes. Calculate ∂f∂t.

a
sest
b
stes
c
se2s
d
test
e
te2s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The chain rule for a multivariable function f(x,y) with two independent variables s and t, where x=x(s,t) and y=y(s,t), can be expressed as follows: ∂f∂t=∂f∂x⋅∂x∂t+∂f∂y⋅∂y∂t

First, we find the partial derivatives of f with respect to x and y: ∂f∂x=2+y,∂f∂y=x

Writing the above results in terms of s and t, we get ∂f∂x=2+tes,∂f∂y=ses.

Next, we take the derivatives of x and y with respect to t, and we get ∂x∂t=0,∂y∂t=es.

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get ∂f∂t=∂f∂x⋅∂x∂t+∂f∂y⋅∂y∂t=(2+tes)(0)+(ses)(es)=se2s.
